cards.title: Vocabulary held once
cards.summary: Each vocabulary block is held once: lookups read the Marlin head's own copy. −0.41 GB GPU memory per 4B checkpoint (Blaze-Q 3.92 GB, = GPTQ W4A16; Blaze-S 2.74 GB), same drift and single-stream speed.
details: Bit-exact against codes × scales and vLLM's own lookup, on vLLM's real Marlin repack, at every 2B and 4B block shape.
GPU weights 4.34 → 3.92 GB; excess 0.00169 → 0.00169; one stream 146.9 → 146.8 tok/s; batched 2,900 → 2,843.
GPU weights 3.15 → 2.74 GB; excess 0.0418 → 0.0418; one stream 174.4 → 174.5 tok/s; batched 2,861 → 2,901.
Per-answer losses move by ~0.0003 nats/token (totals equal), the size of switching body kernels; likely torch.compile fusion, not proven.
₹4.68 (stopped on a compile error, fixed) + ₹75.67 (watcher hung; over the ₹60 cap). Watcher hardened.

cards.title: Blaze-S, corrected
cards.summary: AutoRound's quality at 2.60 GB (−31%): excess loss 0.0418 against 0.0417, one stream 174 tok/s against 151, GPU weights 3.15 GB against 3.92. MMMU within noise.
details: With the published AutoRound body, does Blaze-S keep its quality at 31% less size?
2,598,000,440 B. Excess loss 0.0418 (AutoRound 0.0417), flips 4.97%. One stream 174 tok/s, batched 2,861 (W4A16: 151, 3,128). GPU weights 3.15 GB.
65.8 against AutoRound's 66.9 and BF16's 69.6; paired −1.1 (−3.3 to +1.0) against AutoRound.
Published body copied as is; vocabulary laddered on the multilingual census; 98 vision Linears at 8-bit g128. Rounding only, no calibration.

cards.title: Real 6-bit Blaze-Q
cards.summary: Servable at W4A16's size on vLLM's own 6-bit kernel: drift 0.00169 (= G2b), one stream 147 tok/s against GPTQ's 151. On 8-bit Marlin: 0.00170, 126 tok/s.
details: Does the equal-size 4B Blaze-Q run for real, and how fast?
3,780,277,088 bytes (GPTQ W4A16: 3,780,662,272). Excess loss 0.00169, flips 1.40%, the same as G2b's fake export. GPU weights 4.34 GB (GPTQ 3.92).
vLLM 0.29 picks Humming for the 6-bit groups and Marlin for the 8-bit ones; Humming needed NVRTC's builtins on the library path.
BLAZE_W6_AS_W8=1 repacks the 6-bit codes for 8-bit Marlin: 0.00170, flips 1.40%, 126 tok/s one stream, 2,539 batched, 4.93 GB.

cards.title: Ladder on code and languages
cards.summary: Code is free; other languages cost the English ladder 0.0039 (Thai 0.024). A multilingual census at the same size: 0.0015 (Thai 0.0027), English unchanged. Blaze-Q beats GPTQ 15× on code, 13× on other languages.
details: Does the English-only ladder hurt code or other languages?

Along BF16's answers to HumanEval, MBPP and MGSM in 11 languages (914 answers): English ladder code −0.0003, multilingual 0.0039; multilingual ladder −0.0001 and 0.0015; GPTQ W4A16 0.0303 and 0.0655; Blaze-Q 0.0020 and 0.0051.
Multilingual ladder on BF16's 1,501 English benchmark answers: 0.00030 (English ladder 0.00022).
Rebuild Blaze-Q on the multilingual census.

cards.title: Blaze-Q, multilingual ladder
cards.summary: Rebuild the real 4B Blaze-Q on the multilingual census, then one drift check (English and other languages) before publishing.
details: Thai is most of Blaze-Q's multilingual gap, and the English ladder is most of Thai's.

cards.title: Full suite on the 4B
cards.summary: 12 of 13 tasks within 1 point of BF16; MathVista −1.1 (paired interval −2.6 to +0.5), 0.1 past the mark.
details: Is every task within 1 point of BF16 (MMMU within 2)?
−1.1 against BF16 on the same 1,000 questions, paired interval −2.6 to +0.5: not distinguishable from BF16, but past the 1-point mark. Glaze v2 is −0.4 (−2.2 to +1.5).
By the rule, report the drop as measured. Against Glaze v2, Blaze-Q is level or ahead on 10 of 13 tasks.
r_f7c16f6c on one A30, 16 Oct 08:28–13:21 UTC; the export was rebuilt from G2b's plan and its drift matched G2b's exactly.

cards.title: Ladder add-on
cards.summary: Free on every published export: GPTQ, AutoRound and Glaze v2 each lose 0.86 GB (−23%) with drift unchanged to 0.0001.
details: Does laddering only the vocabulary table of an existing 4-bit export keep its quality?
GPTQ + ladder: one stream 175 tok/s against 151 (+16%); batched 2,912 against 3,126 (−7%); GPU weights 3.47 GB against 3.92.
Glaze v2's quality at 2.91 GB, and any 4-bit Qwen3.5 export 23% smaller, servable today with the blaze-vllm plugin.

cards.title: Vocabulary census
cards.summary: 80,010 of 248,320 rows ever used; the busiest 65,536 hold 99.97% of answer tokens.
details: How much of the vocabulary sits idle?
Training splits only (MATH, GSM8K, ARC, SciQ, HellaSwag, WikiText-2, UltraChat, COCO captions) plus BF16's answers to Glaze v2's training prompts.
65,536 rows at 8-bit g128, 182,784 at 4-bit g128. The 4B table goes from 1.271 GB to 0.413 GB.

cards.title: Is the ladder free?
cards.summary: Excess loss 0.0002 and 0.40% flips, against BF16's 0.35% floor.
details: Does storing idle vocabulary rows at 4 bits cost anything?
Ladder alone: 0.0002 excess loss (mark 0.001). 6-bit body, plain rounding: 0.0048 (mark 0.004, a narrow miss). FFN prices flat: 0.65 against a 0.75 mark, so a 4/8-bit menu is not enough.
The ladder is free; the body needs a 6-bit option.

cards.title: 6-bit body, GPTQ
cards.summary: Excess loss 0.0027 against a 0.003 mark; 0.4% over W4A16's size.
details: Does GPTQ rounding make a 6-bit body pay?
Same 6-bit g128 grid as G1, GPTQ on WikiText-2 training text, no in-domain data.
0.0027 excess loss, 1.76% flips: 1.8× better than plain rounding and 5× below Glaze v2.

cards.title: Does the 2B agree?
cards.summary: Excess loss 0.0005 against W4A16's 0.073 at the same 2.39 GB; panel at BF16's level.
details: At a standard W4A16 export's size, does Blaze-Q (ladder plus an 8-bit body) beat GPTQ W4A16?

cards.title: 4B at W4A16's size
cards.summary: Excess loss 0.0017, 8.5× below Glaze v2, with the vision tower at 8 bits.
details: Can Blaze-Q beat Glaze v2 2.4× at exactly a standard 4-bit export's size?
Vision tower at 8 bits (as Glaze v2 stores it), body at 6 bits with 23 of 64 units at 8, chosen by measured 4-bit prices.
0.0017 excess loss, 1.39% flips, 3,780,086,784 bytes against W4A16's 3,780,662,272.

cards.title: Benchmark panel
details: Is every panel task within 1 point of BF16?
Pass; the next gate is G4, the full suite.

cards.title: Real format in vLLM
cards.summary: The real 2B export serves like the fake one, at W4A16's size: 229 tok/s single-stream.
details: Does vLLM serve the real tiered format as its fake-quantized twin?
Drift 0.00047 real against 0.00046 fake. On disk 2.389 GB (W4A16 2.389). GPU weights 2.86 GB (W4A16 2.52). Single stream 229 tok/s (W4A16 240, BF16 164); batched 7,890 (9,107).

cards.title: 4B at size, vision BF16
cards.summary: Excess loss 0.0071, 2.0× below Glaze v2, short of the 2.4× mark.
details: Two FFN layers had to drop to 4 bits to fit, and the 6-bit prices that chose them were mostly noise.
G2b: the vision tower at 8 bits, and prices ranked at 4 bits.

cards.title: Vocabulary held once
cards.summary: Correct, and at W4A16's memory, but the kernel is 4× slower single-stream. Replaced by the Marlin-layout lookup (V1).
details: Same drift (0.00047). GPU weights 2.53 GB (two copies: 2.86). Single stream 57 tok/s against 229; batched 5,474 against 7,890.
Tune the dequantizing kernel; until then two copies stay the default.

cards.title: Untied 9B check
cards.summary: Tests the method on a model with separate input and output tables.
details: The 9B's vocabulary is 48% of a W4A16 export; the head is laddered and the input table goes to 4 bits.

cards.title: Publish the 2B
cards.summary: Glaze v2 + ladder (2.91 GB) and the real 2B Blaze-Q as private Kiln repos with the vLLM plugin.
details: Both are real, servable today, and keep their quality at fewer bytes.

cards.title: Blaze-S: the smaller 4B
cards.summary: 31% smaller than GPTQ W4A16 (2.60 GB) and 16% faster single-stream, but less accurate: its own 4-bit GPTQ is weaker than the published one. Superseded by Blaze-S, corrected.
details: Is Blaze-S smaller than GPTQ W4A16, as accurate, and at least as fast for a single stream?
2.60 GB on disk against 3.78 (−31%). One stream 174 tok/s against GPTQ's 151 and BF16's 80; batched 2,901 against 3,128 (−7%). GPU weights 3.15 GB against 3.92.
Excess loss 0.090 against the published GPTQ's 0.054; MMLU-Pro (1,001) 67.9 (GPTQ 70.1, BF16 73.6), MATH-500 74.2 (75.8, 83.4), IFEval 75.6 (80.8, 82.3).

Blaze's own GPTQ (WikiText-2 calibration, no activation ordering) is barely better than plain rounding at 4 bits (0.090 against 0.094); the published GPTQ used 512 chat samples. The ladder and the vision tower are not the cause.
Build Blaze-S on the published GPTQ body: same body bytes, ladder and 8-bit vision around it.

cards.title: 6-bit kernel
cards.summary: Correct (error 1e-4) but slow: a decode token's body takes 21 ms against Marlin 4-bit's 4.7 ms and BF16's 9.3 ms.
details: At batch 1 on an A30 it moves about 105 GB/s against Marlin's 500. Batch 256 is 4–6× slower than Marlin.
A first Triton kernel: per-element unpacking and loads that do not saturate memory bandwidth.
Build the 6-bit path on Marlin's own dequantize-in-registers design instead of a new Triton kernel.

cards.title: 6-bit kernel: not needed
cards.summary: vLLM 0.29's bundled Humming kernel serves dense 6-bit groups at 3% below Marlin 4-bit's single-stream speed.
details: The Triton prototype is correct but 4.6× slower than Marlin 4-bit at batch 1.

cards.title: Blaze-Q on 4/8-bit kernels
cards.summary: Excess loss 0.0235 at W4A16's size: 2.3× below GPTQ and 1.8× below AutoRound, but above Glaze v2 (0.0143). The 6-bit option is needed.
details: The published GPTQ export, laddered, with 34 of 64 units re-quantized to 8 bits by measured 4-bit prices; 3.774 GB.
One stream 147 tok/s against GPTQ's 151; GPU weights 4.32 GB.
Confirms G1: with flat sensitivity, 4 and 8 bits cannot match the 6-bit body's 0.0017. A real equal-size Blaze-Q needs the 6-bit kernel.
